title: Cross-stitch robin on linen
subtitle: A classic British garden bird in twelve colours on 28-count linen
excerpt: This robin sits on a branch against a plain linen background, worked in twelve DMC colours on 28-count linen. The design is roughly 60 by 80 stitches and finishes at approximately 11 by 14 cm. Most of the stitching uses full cross-stitch fill; the beak and eye details use two strands of back-stitch.
sourceNotes: Original design. The robin (Erithacus rubecula) is native to Britain and Ireland; colour references from RSPB field guide photography.

glossaryTerms.definition: Two diagonal stitches worked over one Aida square to form a complete X. The second diagonal always crosses the first in the same direction across the whole piece.

content.text: This robin design works up quickly on 28-count linen. Most of the body area is standard
fill; the branch uses long back-stitches; the eye needs a single stitch in white on top of the dark fill.

items.label: Thread
items.value: DMC 920 (rust), 3776 (orange-red), 400 (dark rust), 433 (brown), 3031 (dark brown), 3782 (light mocha), ECRU (cream), 310 (black), 3865 (white), 648 (light grey), 3799 (dark grey), 435 (light brown)

content.text: Prepare the linen and mark the centre.
Overcast or tape the linen edges to prevent fraying. Fold the fabric in quarters and mark the centre with a small pencil cross. Mount in the hoop, keeping the grid square.

Start at the centre of the breast area using DMC 3776. Linen is worked over two threads in each direction. Count two threads across and two threads down for each stitch corner. The breast uses 3776 as the main fill and 920 for the outer shadow edge.
Work the back and head in 433 and 3031, the breast shadow in 400, and the wing and tail feathers in 3782 and 648. Complete each colour section before moving on rather than jumping between colours.
Add the branch last before outlining.
Work the branch in 435 and 3031 using full cross-stitch. The robin's feet grip the branch in 310.
Outline the robin's body in 3799 using two strands. The beak outline and eye ring use 310 in a single strand. Work a single white stitch (3865) as a highlight dot on the eye.

Remove from the hoop and hand-wash in cool water if the fabric has hoop marks. Press face-down on a towel. The linen background can be left unstitched, trimmed to a 5 cm border, and mounted in a 15 × 18 cm frame with white card behind.
